people.name: Ada_Lovelace
people.summary: Ada Lovelace (Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace) was an English mathematician and writer, and the only legitimate child of the poet Lord Byron and Anne Isabella Milbanke. Educated intensively in mathematics and science, she became a close collaborator of Charles Babbage on his Analytical Engine. In 1843 she published an influential translation of Luigi Menabrea’s paper on the machine, supplemented with extensive notes that included a table for computing Bernoulli numbers, often described as the first published computer program, and reflections on how such engines might manipulate symbols beyond arithmetic.

people.name: Alan_Turing
people.summary: Alan Mathison Turing (1912–1954) was an English mathematician, logician, computer scientist, and cryptanalyst. He founded theoretical computer science through his concept of the Turing machine, made decisive contributions to breaking German ciphers at Bletchley Park during World War II, and later worked on early computers and mathematical biology. His life and career were cut short after a 1952 conviction for homosexual acts and subsequent hormone treatment; he died in 1954 from cyanide poisoning.

people.name: Albert_Einstein
people.summary: Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist who developed the theories of special and general relativity and made seminal contributions to quantum theory and statistical physics. His 1905 annus mirabilis papers transformed modern physics, and his mass–energy equivalence relation E = mc² became iconic. Awarded the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for his explanation of the photoelectric effect, he held academic posts in Zurich, Prague, Berlin, and Princeton. A Jewish refugee from Nazi Germany, he became a prominent public intellectual, speaking on pacifism, Zionism, civil liberties, and the dangers of nuclear weapons.

people.name: E._T._A._Hoffmann
people.summary: Ernst Theodor Amadeus Hoffmann (born Ernst Theodor Wilhelm Hoffmann; 24 January 1776 – 25 June 1822) was a German Romantic writer of fantasy and gothic horror, as well as a jurist, composer, music critic, and illustrator. His tales, including "The Nutcracker and the Mouse King," "The Sandman," and "The Golden Pot," were central to German Romanticism and later inspired works such as Tchaikovsky's ballet The Nutcracker and Offenbach's opera The Tales of Hoffmann.

people.name: Edsger_W._Dijkstra
people.summary: Edsger W. Dijkstra (1930–2002) was a Dutch computer scientist and pioneer of structured programming, operating systems, and algorithmic thinking. The first professional programmer in the Netherlands, he developed Dijkstra’s shortest-path algorithm, contributed to ALGOL 60 and the first ALGOL 60 compiler, designed the THE operating system, and wrote hundreds of influential essays and technical reports that helped shape modern computer science.

people.name: Emmy Noether
people.summary: Amalie Emmy Noether was a German mathematician who fundamentally transformed abstract algebra and proved Noether's theorems linking symmetries to conservation laws in physics. A leading figure at Göttingen, she developed deep theories of rings, fields, and algebras, and later taught in the United States at Bryn Mawr College while conducting research at the Institute for Advanced Study.

people.name: Erich_Kästner
people.summary: Emil Erich Kästner was a German writer, poet, screenwriter, and satirist, best known for his witty, socially observant poems and for children's classics such as Emil and the Detectives, Lisa and Lottie, and The Flying Classroom. A key figure of Weimar-era Neue Sachlichkeit, he remained in Germany under National Socialism, where his books were banned and burned while he continued to publish some works abroad and write screenplays under a pseudonym. After 1945 he settled in Munich, working as editor, cabaret writer, radio author, and children's author, and received the Hans Christian Andersen Award in 1960 for his autobiography When I Was a Little Boy.

people.name: Franz_Kafka
people.summary: Franz Kafka (3 July 1883 – 3 June 1924) was a German-language Jewish Czech writer whose novels and stories, blending realism and the fantastique, explore themes of alienation, bureaucracy, and existential anxiety. Born in Prague, he trained and worked as a lawyer and insurance official while writing largely unpublished fiction that later became central to 20th‑century literature, including The Metamorphosis, The Trial, and The Castle.

people.name: Friedensreich_Hundertwasser
people.summary: Friedrich Stowasser, better known as Friedensreich Regentag Dunkelbunt Hundertwasser, was an Austrian visual artist and architect noted for vivid colors, biomorphic forms, and ecological advocacy. He opposed straight lines and standardization, and later settled in the Far North of New Zealand, where he lived and worked for much of his life.

people.name: Grace_Hopper
people.summary: Grace Brewster Hopper was an American computer scientist, mathematician, and U.S. Navy rear admiral. A pioneer of computer programming, she helped develop the Harvard Mark I, devised the theory of machine‑independent programming languages, and led creation of early compilers including FLOW‑MATIC, which strongly influenced COBOL. She served for decades in the Navy, shaping standards for programming languages and computer systems.

people.name: Hedy_Lamarr
people.summary: Hedy Lamarr (born Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler) was an Austrian-born American film actress and inventor. Rising to fame in Europe with the controversial film Ecstasy (1933), she later became a Hollywood star in such films as Algiers (1938), Boom Town (1940), White Cargo (1942), and Samson and Delilah (1949). During the Second World War she co‑invented, with composer George Antheil, a frequency‑hopping "Secret Communication System" for torpedo guidance, an important precursor to modern spread-spectrum technologies used in wireless communication.

people.name: Henry_II
people.summary: Henry II (6 May 973 – 13 July 1024), also known as Saint Henry, was Duke of Bavaria, King of the Romans, King of Italy, and Holy Roman Emperor. The last ruler of the Ottonian dynasty, he consolidated royal power north of the Alps, relied heavily on the Church and episcopal administration, promoted monastic reform, founded the Diocese of Bamberg, and fought major wars against Bolesław I of Poland and rivals in Italy. Deeply pious and childless, he was canonized in 1146.
primaryRoles: King of Germany (King of the Romans)

people.name: Thomas_Cromwell
people.summary: Thomas Cromwell (c.1485 – 28 July 1540) was an English statesman and lawyer who rose from humble origins in Putney to become chief minister to King Henry VIII. A principal architect of the English Reformation, he masterminded the break with Rome, the royal supremacy over the Church of England, major administrative and financial reforms, and the dissolution of the monasteries. Created Earl of Essex in 1540, he fell from favour after arranging Henry’s marriage to Anne of Cleves and was executed for treason and heresy on Tower Hill.
